newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia welcomes new Japan rice tender timing.
newsitem.headline: Australia welcomes new Japan rice tender timing.

text.p: An earlier than usual tender by Japan for imported rice was good news for Australia, the Australian Rice Growers' Co-operative said on Wednesday.
This would be especially so if it confirmed a policy shift toward more a equitable spread of purchases over the year, managing director Jim Kennedy said in a statement.
Kennedy was commenting on a decision by the Japanese government Food Agency to hold a tender on May 28 for 7,000 tonnes of rice under the simultaneous buying and selling (SBS) import system.
The timing was earlier than in previous years and would increase the number of SBS tenders in 1997 to four from three, he said.

The timing of rice import tenders was raised as a significant issue with Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto by Australian Prime Minister John Howard late last year in Tokyo and again during Hashimoto's Australia visit this week, he said.

Japan imports rice through large-volume Minimum Access tenders operated by the Food Agency and through relatively low-volume SBS tenders, which involve direct sale by suppliers to companies licenced by the Food Agency.
Australia has argued strongly that tenders for foreign rice should begin early in the year and be spread more regularly throughout it, Kennedy said.

The Australian rice industry had availability of high quality new season rice from March each year, while other potential suppliers did not have equivalent high quality product until September, he said.
"Australia has historically been disadvantaged by Japan's procedures which have repeatedly scheduled tenders from September," he said.
A real impact for Australia would require a similar shift in scheduling policy for Minimum Access tenders, Kennedy said.
Australia exported about 90,000 tonnes of rice to Japan last year.
